blocks.c: Nine racks down. Tall box. Four inches of dust on the shelf beside it and none on the box, because it was still being added to.
And they were not sealed, because a held dispute is not sealed, and one of them was labelled in the clerk's small neat hand:
Item: the face of the night technician, 2019. Disputed in writing by M. Dalisay, 14 August 2019. Held.
She had filed. Of course she had filed. She writes her logs properly; she told me so in a car park.

Twenty-two years of a woman who never once got in the elevator, quietly disputing in ink every single thing that building took off her, and putting the disputes in a maintenance log where nobody would ever read them.
I sat down on the floor of an impossible warehouse and laughed until I nearly threw up.
Because here is what that means.
Wen filed for four years. Mrs. Dalisay has filed for twenty-two. I have filed for eleven days.
Clause fourteen says a held dispute needs a hearing, and a hearing needs two parties present and signing.
There had never been three of us before.
I got out my book and I wrote, in the biggest letters I have ever written in a log:
04:31. I demand a hearing under clause fourteen. Parties: R. Oduya (caretaker-elect), W. Aguilar (caretaker), M. Dalisay (witness to the 1974 renewal). All three present and able to sign.
And every single light in that warehouse came on at once.
